Block diagram of the data acquisition system. The load MOSFETs are two IRF540N (PV1 on PWM pin 5, PV2 on PWM pin 12) and one IRLZ44N (TEG, PWM pin 8); the numbers are Arduino pin numbers. The two INA219 modules (addresses 0x40 and 0x41), the ADS1115 (address 0x48) and the real-time clock share the I²C bus. The ADS1115 is one chip, drawn twice: it measures the voltage and current of the TEG string and the BPW34 signal. The MAX6675 modules use a separate software SPI bus with one chip-select line each, and the microSD card uses the hardware SPI bus.

Variable-load circuit of a PV channel (PV1 and PV2 are identical). A PWM output of the Arduino (pin 5 or 12) drives the gate (G) of the IRF540N through a 10 kΩ resistor. A 10 µF capacitor from the gate to ground smooths the PWM signal, and a resistor from the gate to ground (two 47 kΩ resistors in series, 94 kΩ) holds the gate low when no signal is present. The current of the panel passes through the 0.1 Ω shunt inside the INA219 and then through the drain (D) and the source (S) of the MOSFET to ground (GND). A 10 µF capacitor is fitted across the terminals of the panel.

Variable-load circuit of the TEG channel. A PWM output of the Arduino (pin 8) drives the gate (G) of the IRLZ44N through a 220 Ω resistor, with a 10 µF capacitor and a 47 kΩ resistor from the gate to ground. The current of the TEG string flows through the drain (D) and the source (S) and through the 1.3 Ω shunt (measured with a multimeter) to ground (GND). A0 and A1 are channels of the ADS1115: A0 reads the voltage of the TEG string and A1 the voltage across the shunt. A 10 µF capacitor is fitted across the terminals of the TEG string.
Photographs of the sweep circuits in two views. The load MOSFETs of the PV channels are IRF540N.

Measurement cycle of the data acquisition system. Between sweeps the panels are at open circuit (PWM = 0) and one record with the eight temperatures is taken every minute. A sweep of the PWM value from 0 to 255 is started about every 15 minutes (15.1 minutes on average, Section 3.4.3); no temperatures are recorded while it runs, so the temperature at the time of a sweep is interpolated between the records before and after it (Section 3.7.1).

Circuit of the BPW34 irradiance sensor. The photodiode is reverse biased, with its cathode at +Vcc (5 V, nominal). The photocurrent flows through six 220 Ω resistors in series (1.32 kΩ) to ground (GND), and the voltage across the resistors is read by channel A2 of the ADS1115. The circuit was the same on all days.
Experimental set-up. (a) Baseline days: the two panels, both bare. (b) Hybrid days: the data acquisition electronics next to the panels. (c) Overview of the set-up. The panels lay flat on a table.

Data processing from the raw files to the results. The sweep file of each day (SMMDD.csv) is fitted sweep by sweep by batch_process.py, which gives the I–V and P–V figures and the summary tables of the PV1, PV2 and TEG parameters. The one-minute file (VMMDD.csv) is calibrated (Section 3.3.4) and handled by batch_temperature.py, which gives the temperature figures and the temperature summary; its temperatures are interpolated to the middle of each sweep (Section 3.7.1). The paired quantities are then compared through ratios and temperature differences. MMDD is the month and the day.
